tagline: An app manager for your household's own machines
brief: HomersLab installs and looks after a household's self-hosted apps on the household's own Linux machines: one household account for every app, private by default with no router ports, backups with a restore test every week, and kids see only kid-safe apps. Open source (Apache-2.0). Named after Homer's Odyssey, the long journey home. It is for the household admin who sets it up and for the family who open their apps every day.
criteria: Success: recognisable at 16 px; works in one colour and reversed; works as a rounded app icon; one primary colour plus a neutral, light and dark. Never: Homer Simpson, a donut, a cyber-security shield. Clearly apart from the Homer dashboard's donut, Home Assistant's house, Runtipi's tipi and Umbrel's umbrella.

concepts.name: Homeward
concepts.idea: The Odyssey's ship, whose yard and square sail form a little house: home, sailing home.
rationale: Answers direction 1: one silhouette reads as a ship and as a house
Square-rigged like the ships on Greek vases; no one in the category has a ship
Friendly and calm as an app icon, nothing like a security badge
Risk: at 16 px the roof greys out; some may read a houseboat or an ark

concepts.name: Lyre
concepts.idea: Homer's lyre, calm and round. In the Odyssey the master proves he is home by stringing his bow as easily as a bard strings a lyre.
rationale: The most direct tie to Homer; no app manager uses a lyre
The bow-and-lyre scene gives sign-in a meaning without a shield
Risks: among photo and media apps it reads as a music app; at 16 px it becomes a cup with horns

concepts.name: Harbour H
concepts.idea: An H for Home, Homer and Harbour: the crossbar is a hull and a sail rises in the counter. The ship, safe home.
rationale: Answers direction 3: an H built from a hull and a sail; its lower counter is a doorway
Strongest small: a crisp H at 16 px that becomes a boat from 24 px
Works as a monogram, an app icon and a pattern (hull, sail, H)
Risk: letter marks need exposure; the sail is the one detail that makes it ours

concepts.name: Wordmark
concepts.idea: HomersLab in a calm literary serif; the r carries a small sail, which also reads as the apostrophe of Homer's.
rationale: Answers direction 5: the name does the work, nothing new to learn
A serif stands apart among the category's geometric sans wordmarks; warm and bookish, like the poet
Risk: weakest small; the favicon falls back to a plain serif H
Risk: the sail-apostrophe may lead people to write Homer's Lab

recommendation: C, Harbour H. It is the strongest at 16 px and as an app icon, it is ownable (the letter people already link to the name, plus a sail nobody else has), and it carries both halves of the story: home (the H, its doorway) and the journey (hull and sail). Pair it with the Figtree lockup, or with D's serif wordmark for a more literary voice. If you would rather lead with a picture, A is the best answer to 'a ship that reads as a house'.
next_steps: Choose a direction, or name what you like in each.
Refine it: optical corrections, a 16 px cut, the custom wordmark, colour (Clay and a warm neutral, light and dark).
Kit: lockups, favicon, PWA and app icons, a one-page usage guide.
Before the name goes public: trademark search (EUIPO, Swissreg, USPTO) for the name and the mark.
